issues.legal_issue: A High Court cannot quash a Union Government order over which it lacks territorial jurisdiction.
material_facts: The petition sought a writ quashing the Union Government’s order concerning the disputed mining area.
The High Court lacked territorial jurisdiction over the Union Government.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not quash the Union Government’s order.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226 of the Constitution, the High Court could not issue certiorari to quash an order of an authority over which it did not exercise territorial jurisdiction. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenges_union_ord: A party brings a constitutional writ petition seeking to quash an order made by the Union Government.
predicates.union_order_maker_outside_high_court_ter: The authority that made the challenged order is outside the territorial jurisdiction of the High Court.

issues.definition: When a constitutional writ challenges a Union Government order made by an authority outside the High Court’s territorial jurisdiction, the High Court cannot quash that order.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot direct a State Government to grant a benefit contrary to an operative Union Government order before that order is set aside.
material_facts: The petition also sought a direction that the disputed mining lease be granted to the appellant.
The Union Government’s order directed that the disputed area be made available for a lease to another applicant, and that order had not been set aside.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not grant the requested direction while the Union Government’s order remained in force.
issues.legal_principle: The requested direction could not be granted until the Union Government’s order was set aside. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.constitutional_writ_seeks_state_action: A party brings a constitutional writ petition seeking to require a State Government to take a particular action.
predicates.operative_union_order_conflicts_with_req: An operative Union Government order directs or requires action inconsistent with the action sought from the State Government.

issues.definition: When a constitutional writ seeks State Government action that conflicts with an operative Union Government order, the requested direction is unavailable until that order is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A Union Government review application remains pending when the earlier communication does not dispose of it and the matter continues to be treated as under consideration.
material_facts: A third party had applied to the Union Government for review of the State Government’s decision.
The Union Government’s earlier letter directed a reduction in the licensed area and that the remaining area be opened for regrant, but did not state how the review application was being disposed of.
Later letters indicated that the matter remained under consideration.
The Union Government subsequently made an order cancelling the State Government’s earlier decision and directing a lease grant, provided the third party was otherwise eligible.
issues.conclusion: The review application had not been disposed of when the Union Government made its later order.
issues.legal_principle: The effect of the earlier communication had to be assessed from its terms and the subsequent correspondence; the letter directing changes to the licensed area did not itself dispose of the review application under Rule 57 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1949. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.administrative_review_proceeding: A government authority is considering an application to review an earlier administrative decision.
predicates.prior_communication_did_not_dispose_of_r: An earlier communication gave directions concerning the underlying matter but did not state that the review application was disposed of.
predicates.later_communications_showed_continued_co: Later communications indicated that the reviewing authority continued to consider the matter.

issues.definition: In an administrative review proceeding, the application remains pending when the earlier communication did not dispose of it and later communications show continued consideration.

issues.legal_issue: A State Government’s decision to grant a mining lease is subject to the Union Government’s order on review, and the State Government implements that order.
material_facts: The State Government had power under the applicable rules to grant the mining lease.
The Union Government directed the State Government to grant the disputed area to the third party, provided that party was otherwise eligible.
The State Government acted in accordance with that direction.
issues.conclusion: The State Government’s grant was subject to the Union Government’s review order, which remained the final order; the State Government merely effectuated it.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Mineral Concession Rules, including Rule 57, the State Government’s lease decision was subject to the Union Government’s order on review. The State Government was required to carry out that order, which remained final. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.reviewable_mining_concession_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a mining concession governed by a scheme that permits review by the Union Government.
predicates.state_lease_decision_subject_to_union_re: The State Government’s power to decide whether to grant a mining lease is subject to the Union Government’s order on review.
predicates.union_government_directed_lease_grant: The Union Government directed the State Government to grant the lease, subject to the proposed recipient being otherwise eligible.

issues.definition: In a reviewable mining-concession proceeding, when the State Government’s lease decision is subject to Union Government review and the Union Government directs a grant, the State Government’s action effectuates the final Union Government order.
